correctness.rationale: The exact circumradius identity follows from Euclidean chord and area formulas. The determinant-two angular torus map pushes Haar to product Haar, proving the three independent factors. An arcsine variable change gives the normalized full density and Euler-hypergeometric Mellin moments; Morse-local pushforward around precisely three saddles of each index gives both explicit one-sided square-root density coefficients; the two definite extrema give exact leading endpoint ball-volume constants. Fourier orthogonality proves the log-radius dilogarithm variance and strict inversion. Fixed axes and all domains are explicit. The packaged standalone checker passed 1845 direct geometric, integral, Hessian, inversion and Monte Carlo tests, supplementary to analytic proof.

value.rationale: The Euclidean circumradius of three independent ellipse-boundary points is a canonical natural invariant. A nontrivial degree-two torus covering yields exact independence of three pairwise midpoint speed factors. Their complete law has two internal geometric caustics with explicit inequivalent coefficients, and two simple population log-radius moments determine both semiaxes. This is a structural complete classification and natural inverse shape signature, not a routine fixed-number computation or trivial restatement of a known special function.
